title: SpaceX Prices $40B GPU Bond Deal at Up to 8.75%

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Elon Musk's aerospace firm has finalized the cost of capital for its newest equipment credit facility, which will fund the acquisition of next-generation computer chips. SpaceX priced the bonds for the $40B arrangement at interest rates of up to 8.75% to secure the hardware needed for its terrestrial artificial intelligence compute buildout.

The master finance lease with Apollo Global Management will be used to purchase Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs, with equipment deliveries scheduled for the first half of 2027. The deal is managed through a special purpose vehicle to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet and is scheduled to close by the end of 2026. The company is using its investment-grade credit rating, supported by Starlink and rocket launch revenue, to access financing that Musk says is now nearly unavailable to smaller "neocloud" providers.

selectedTweets.text:
$SPCX - SPACEX SIGNS $40 BILLION GPU FINANCING DEAL WITH APOLLO

SpaceX has entered into a binding commitment for a master finance lease with Apollo Global Management ($APO ), according to an SEC filing.

Apollo will purchase GPU pods and related equipment and lease them to SpaceX, with aggregate scheduled principal payments expected to total $40 billion.

The agreement is expected to close before year-end 2026.

The key takeaway: SpaceX is securing large-scale GPU infrastructure through lease financing, highlighting the enormous capital requirements of AI expansion.

selectedTweets.text:
APOLLO'S SPACEX BET: @elonmusk's firm in a regulatory filing this morning disclosed that Apollo will be responsible for buying and leasing GPUs, with roughly a five-year lease term totalling $40 billion.

It's another really large affirmation of the AI buildout, even if the industry is facing rotations more largely. It also shows you how much dry powder is still on the sidelines for just a single-issuer deal, with one major credit counterparty (though wouldn't be surprised to see Apollo syndicate the deal). Think this is really just the tip of the iceberg with how much private capital will continue to flow in.
